objective: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.
objectiveFingerprint: become campaign card day eligible emi history no plan purchases

questions.text: When you say you want more EMI-eligible purchases to convert, do you mean you want more transactions converted, or more value/amount converted into EMI — even if that means fewer but larger conversions?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: Design targets volume: broad reach, easy low-friction conversions, message tuned to make converting feel simple regardless of ticket size.
contingency.ifB: Design targets value: prioritise larger eligible transactions and customers with bigger EMI-eligible balances, even if the total count of conversions is smaller.
contingency.ifUnknown: Default to counting conversions but flag that this favours small-ticket conversions, and ask again once the first run's data is in.

questions.text: Have you noticed any pattern in who already converts an eligible purchase to EMI on their own, or is that something you don't track?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: Use the named pattern to decide who the campaign should focus on first.
contingency.ifB: Treat it as unknown and design the first run to also surface which segment converts, rather than assuming one.

questions.text: What do you believe is stopping the rest of the eligible purchases from being converted?
questions.author: agent

contingency.ifA: Build messaging and timing around the specific reason given (e.g. unaware of the option, cost concern, timing of the offer window).
contingency.ifB: If they say they don't know, widen the first run to test more than one plausible barrier rather than designing around a guess.

facts.statement: They have no campaign history, and said so themselves. There is no conversion rate, benchmark, baseline or past result to ask for — this run IS the first one.
They asked for a plan over 7 days. That is the window the campaign has to work inside — do not ask how long they want.

limitations: Stated as unavailable by the user: We want more EMI-eligible card purchases to become EMI. We have no campaign history. I need a 7 day plan.

dimensions.name: transaction amount
dimensions.rationale: It is the one pattern the manager has actually seen in who converts today. Since success is measured by count of conversions and high-ticket transactions already self-convert, the real headroom for additional count sits in sub-₹10,000 eligible transactions — this changes where the campaign's effort should concentrate.
dimensions.note: Manager reports ₹10,000+ transactions convert more often already; the campaign will cover the full eligible base but is designed expecting most of the incremental count to come from below that threshold.

dimensions.name: purchase channel (online checkout vs in-store/POS swipe)
dimensions.rationale: Online checkouts often surface a merchant EMI offer directly, which could explain part of the awareness gap the manager suspects, versus a POS swipe where no such prompt ever appears.
dimensions.note: Not raised by the manager and not something this post-purchase nudge needs to vary by, since the message reaches the customer after the transaction regardless of where it happened. Carried as a possible explanation to watch in results, not a split to design around now.

successCriteria: More transactions converted into EMI — a count of conversions, not the rupee value converted. Explicitly chosen over a value-based measure.

contextChecked.source: knowledge base — EMI request expiry window (auth-triggered EMI stays open up to 7 days, P-003)

converters.shape: Transactions of ₹10,000 or more convert to EMI on their own more often than smaller eligible transactions.

candidates.why: The campaign manager has observed these convert more often without prompting.

barriers.statement: Customers don't realise a given purchase actually qualifies to be converted to EMI, so they never act on it.
